title: The Clam House, Monk and leaving New Orleans at nineteen
summary: He recalls the Clam House after-hours piano scene and talks about the ten years away, 1926 to 1936.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah, I knew Pop. I knew Fats Duarte was pretty good. We used to go up to the hall and after hours and time, you know, I'll tell you about that place called the Clam House. They had a big colored piano playing piano and all the piano players used to come up and sit and play. Like Willie the Lion used to come in and sometime I would come in. Not too much of them coming on the floor. But they had a different kind of play that she didn't play, I mean you know, Phil will play. That's wrong. Oh God. Moke was up there too, come to think of it. Moke who? Hazel. Oh yeah.
Well he came to New York with that band, I'm trying to see, was it that band?
Yeah, I think he came up with that band from New York that time I was doing, I think. It was some band, I can't think of who it was. I can't think of it, he came to New York.
Well Monk would tell me about Sidney Aarland and Louie.
Oh yeah, he knew much better than me. Yeah. I mean sure Monk knew.

Well you see, like I said, about me leaving here when I was just, if I had stayed around New Orleans when I was 19 and stayed here and worked there for 10 years, you know what I mean? I was out for between 20 and 30, I came back when I was 30 years old, 1936. But I mean that 10 years that I left there, that's why I had met Sharky before I went away and that's why I knew Sharky in New York. I mean there were a lot of other guys, some guys I met right before I left and I didn't see them for a long time, you know what I mean?
Well a lot of guys had gone for years, like Joey Bruney's would have been too old even because he was a grown man.
